XRAY-1002760 - GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr (esbuild < 0.28.1)
- Missing binary integrity verification in esbuild's Deno module enables RCE via NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY manipulation.
- NOT introduced by this PR: affects esbuild@0.27.x pulled transitively via tsx@4.21.0 (ark-broker, ark-cli) and vite@7.3.2 (ark-dashboard). No package-lock.json was modified in this PR.
- Exploitation requires the attacker to control NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY during a Deno binary download at build time. Does not affect production runtime — esbuild is a dev-only toolchain dep, not deployed in any container.
- Fix requires tsx upgrade (4.x→5.x or newer minor that allows esbuild@~0.28.0) and vite upgrade (7.x→8.x) across three packages; tracked separately.

XRAY-97724 - CVE-2018-20225
- An issue was discovered in pip (all versions) because it installs the version with the highest version number, even if the user had intended to obtain a private package from a private index. This only affects use of the --extra-index-url option, and exploitation requires that the package does not already exist in the public index (and thus the attacker can put the package there with an arbitrary version number). NOTE: it has been reported that this is intended functionality and the user is responsible for using --extra-index-url securely.
- NOT EXPLOITABLE in Ark: Ark uses uv (not pip) for Python dependency management in all production services (ark-api, ark-mcp, simple-agent, retrieval-service, tool templates).
- Evidence: All Python Dockerfiles use "uv sync --frozen" for dependency installation. pip is only present in base images and used to bootstrap uv itself ("pip install uv"), never for --extra-index-url operations.
- No fix available: This is considered intended pip functionality per official response. Using uv eliminates the attack vector entirely.

XRAY-1051070 - CVE-2026-73086 / GHSA-xwg4-73v4-xw9w (nanoid integer overflow)
- nanoid(size) coerced size to a signed 32-bit int; 2147483648 wrapped to -2147483648 and corrupted the CSPRNG poolOffset, making tokens the deterministic string "uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu" until restart. Fixed on the 3.x line in 3.3.12 and on the 5.x line in 5.1.11.
- FALSE POSITIVE: Ark ships patched nanoid — 3.3.17 (docs) and 3.3.18 (tools/ark-cli, services/ark-landing-page, services/ark-dashboard), both above the 3.3.12 fix. Xray's "fixed" metadata lists only 5.1.11 and omits 3.3.12, so it flags the patched 3.3.x releases anyway.
- Verified at source, not just advisory data: nanoid 3.3.18 fillPool() still guards "if (bytes < 0) throw new RangeError", and nanoid()/random() feed it "(size |= 0)". The exploit input wraps to a negative value and is rejected before poolOffset is touched. Guard is unchanged since 3.3.12 (3.3.12->3.3.18 only relaxed the upper 1024 cap in the ESM build); not a regression. Matches OSV: affected = 3.3.0-3.3.11 and 4.0.0-5.1.10; 3.3.12-3.3.18 not affected.
- Cannot upgrade to 5.1.11: nanoid is transitive, pulled only by postcss, which pins nanoid ^3.3.x (3.x line) even at its latest 8.5.26. nanoid 5.x is ESM-only and would break postcss's CommonJS require() and every Next.js/CLI build.
- Remove this entry if Xray corrects its fixed-version metadata, or if nanoid moves onto a genuinely affected line.

XRAY-1090872 - CVE-2026-93687 (braces@3.0.3)
- Stack overflow in braces' recursive AST walkers, which lack depth guards: a deeply nested brace pattern under the character limit exhausts the call stack and crashes the process with an uncaught RangeError.
- No fix available: 3.0.3 is the latest published release (https://github.com/micromatch/braces/issues/73 — upstream confirms no patched version exists yet).
- Not runtime-exploitable in Ark: braces is pulled in transitively via micromatch/chokidar (file-watching and glob matching for build tooling — Vite/Next.js/Jest/ESLint), never invoked on attacker-controlled input in any deployed service.
- Remove this entry once micromatch/chokidar ship a release depending on a patched braces, or braces itself patches the recursion guard.

XRAY-1092077 - CVE-2026-93690 (uri-js@4.4.1)
- DoS in uri-js's removeDotSegments(): loops infinitely on a path segment starting with a Unicode line/paragraph separator, blocking the Node.js event loop until heap exhaustion.
- No fix available: 4.4.1 is the latest published release.
- Not runtime-exploitable in Ark: uri-js is pulled in transitively via ajv (JSON schema validation used by ESLint's own config validation and other build tooling), not invoked on attacker-controlled input by any deployed service.
- Remove this entry once ajv depends on a patched uri-js release, or uri-js itself patches removeDotSegments.

XRAY-1092092 - CVE-2026-93749 (source-map-js@1.2.1)
- DoS in source-map-js: fails to validate the per-section offset line value in indexed source maps, so an attacker-supplied source map with an extremely large offset causes synchronous event-loop blocking.
- No fix available: 1.2.1 is the latest published release.
- Not runtime-exploitable in Ark: source-map-js is pulled in transitively via postcss/magicast/css-tree/@tailwindcss/node (CSS/build-time source-map processing during `next build`/`docs build`), not something any deployed service parses from external input at runtime.
- Remove this entry once postcss/magicast/css-tree depend on a patched source-map-js release, or source-map-js itself adds offset validation.

XRAY-1092096 - CVE-2026-93753 (deepmerge@4.3.1)
- Prototype-poisoning in deepmerge's mergeObject(): fails to validate keys being written to the target object, letting a malicious source object in a merge operation inject properties onto the result's prototype.
- No fix available: 4.3.1 is the latest published release.
- Not runtime-exploitable in Ark: deepmerge is pulled in transitively via jest-config (test-runner configuration merging), a dev/test-only dependency never present in any deployed container and never merging attacker-controlled objects.
- Remove this entry once jest-config depends on a patched deepmerge release, or deepmerge itself validates merge keys.
